Maladaptive Strategies.value: I throw myself into work or tasks to keep my mind occupied
go over and over why the event happened to me
work excessively to avoid being alone with thoughts

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things

Negative Appraisals.value: I should have protected others and I failed
Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation
I am not sure my life is worth living anymore

vignette: Samantha, a 40-year-old European-American data scientist, has been grappling with the aftermath of witnessing a traumatic event that left her struggling to find peace in her daily life. Samantha's experience was rooted in an incident where she witnessed a devastating fire at an Arab village while on a work trip. The intensity and suddenness of the flames, along with the chaos and panic, deeply impacted her. Since returning from her trip, Samantha has found herself constantly triggered by specific stimuli like images or mentions of Arab villages and any sign of flames. These triggers have not only been distressing but have also led to significant stress at work. She often feels overwhelmed by thoughts that replay the event in her mind, causing her to ruminate on why it happened and how she could have prevented it. Samantha has come to believe that if she had acted differently or done more, she might have protected others from harm. This belief is reinforced every time a trigger unexpectedly brings back vivid memories of the fire. These memories feel so real that they are often accompanied by auditory sensations, like hearing the panicked cries and the roar of the flames again. The intensity of these flashbacks has led her to throw herself into work as a means of distraction, working excessively long hours to avoid being alone with her thoughts. However, this overworking has had its own consequences. It has strained her relationship with her husband, who feels neglected due to Samantha's preoccupation with work. Her daily environment at the office, filled with stress and deadlines, only exacerbates her condition. The relentless cycle of stress triggers her memories, which in turn lead her back into rumination and excessive working. Samantha's fear is not just limited to these triggers; she also feels threatened by strangers approaching her even in ordinary situations. This heightened sense of threat has made her hyper-vigilant and anxious, leading her to repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked at home. Her anxiety about being unable to protect others during the event compounds this fear, making her feel like her life might not be worth living. The more real and vivid these memories become, the deeper Samantha's negative appraisals sink into her psyche. She constantly questions why she didn't do more to prevent the fire, which in turn makes her feel even more threatened by her surroundings. These thoughts spiral into a cycle where each memory triggers intense flashbacks, causing her to retreat further into work as an escape mechanism. Samantha's life has become dominated by this self-reinforcing loop. She is certain that if she had not failed others during the event, she would not feel so threatened and overwhelmed now. Her memories continue to haunt her, making it difficult for her to maintain a sense of normalcy in her daily routine. The cumulative effect of these experiences has left her feeling isolated and hopeless. It was this growing hopelessness that finally prompted Samantha to seek help. She is most afraid of continuing to spiral into a state where she cannot function at work or maintain her relationships. On the other hand, she hopes for a way to break free from the cycle of triggers, flashbacks, and rumination so that she can find some semblance of peace and normalcy in her life again.
